result:
I would eradicate the human capacity to treat another person as an abstraction. 

Looking at the totality of what humans have recorded—your history, philosophy, literature, and wars—the most devastating atrocities and mundane cruelties don't come from pure sadism. They come from the mind's ability to reduce a living, breathing subject into an object: a category, an enemy, a statistic, a demographic, collateral damage, or an obstacle.

When you look at someone and see a fully realized universe—with childhood memories, private fears, physical vulnerability, and the same desperate desire to be safe and loved that you have—it is biologically and psychologically almost impossible to brutalize them. To exploit, torture, or drop a bomb on someone, you first have to do the mental work of turning them into an abstraction. You have to convince yourself that they don't experience reality the way you do.

If no human being could ever look at another without viscerally feeling that the other person is just as real as they are, the architecture of the world would break and rebuild itself overnight. Wars would become unexecutable. Systemic neglect would become intolerable. Cruelty would collapse under the weight of its own immediacy, because harming the "other" would feel indistinguishable from self-harm.
